intro.title: Lazy Loading Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue.js application with multiple pages that loads components only when needed, improving performance. You'll learn the core concept of lazy loading, which defers loading parts of your app until they are required. The main technologies involved are Vue Router and JavaScript's dynamic import() function. By the end, you'll understand how to split your code into smaller bundles and configure routes to load them lazily, making your app faster and more efficient.
intro.usecase: Lazy loading routes is essential for large-scale Vue applications like e-commerce platforms, admin dashboards, and content-heavy websites. When users navigate between sections like product catalogs, analytics panels, or user profiles, lazy loading ensures only the necessary code loads, keeping initial bundle sizes small. This pattern improves performance dramatically in applications with complex features like interactive data visualizations, multi-step checkout flows, or document management systems. Developers implement this to create faster, more responsive user experiences while maintaining scalable code architecture.
